title: Enterprise onboarding playbook: escalation, integration, health & QBR
author: Maya Rodriguez
body:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates the standard processes, checklists, and runbooks used by Redwood Inference Customer Success and Support teams for enterprise onboarding. It covers three tightly coupled domains: integration guidance, escalation procedures for incidents and product gaps, and the operational health check / QBR cadence used to measure ongoing success. The intent is to provide a single, consumable reference for CSMs, Solutions Engineers, Support Engineers, and SREs during the first 90–180 days of an enterprise engagement and on an ongoing basis.

Scope:

- Applies to all enterprise customers (Dedicated and Private deployments, and Hosted customers on enterprise plans).
- Covers technical integration, operational readiness, escalation workflow for Sev 1/2/3 issues, and quarterly business reviews (QBRs) and monthly health checks.
- Exclusions: sales contract negotiation and billing disputes (see finance-and-legal).

Quick summary of responsibilities:

- Customer Success Manager (CSM): primary relationship owner, QBR lead, coordinates cross-functional actions.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): integration lead during onboarding, owns technical runbook handover.
- Support Engineer (SEng): triage and initial support for incidents; escalates to SRE/runtime as needed.
- SRE / Eng-Serving-Runtime: incident response, capacity and reliability remediation, root cause analysis (RCA).
- Escalation Manager: coordinates multi-team response for Sev1/2 incidents, external communications.

Pre-onboarding checklist (must be completed before week 0):

- Account & security: customer account created, contract countersigned, security questionnaire completed, NDA in place if required.
- Network & access: IP allowlist entries, VPC peering details, KMS/HSM integration plan (if Private).
- Data & compliance: data residency requirements documented, logging/audit expectations agreed.
- Technical onboarding: API key issued, test workspace created, sample data/ingestion plan provided.
- Stakeholders: CSM, SE, SEng, primary engineering contact, security contact identified.

Integration guide (high-level steps):

1. Kickoff (Week 0–1):
   - Run onboarding kickoff with stakeholders. Review architecture, traffic profile, and SLOs.
   - Deliver integration plan and timeline.

2. Environment readiness (Week 1–2):
   - For Dedicated/Private: confirm GPU pool sizing, autoscaling policy, and network connectivity.
   - For Hosted: validate rate limits, quotas, and billing settings.

3. API integration (Week 2–4):
   - Provide SDK examples and sample prompts for customer workload.
   - Validate authentication and token rotation processes.
   - Confirm streaming and function/tool-calling behavior if used.

4. Performance validation (Week 3–6):
   - Run representative load tests (see Performance validation checklist table).
   - Capture latency and throughput baselines, KV-cache hit rates, and token cost estimates.

5. Handover & runbooks (Week 4–8):
   - Deliver runbooks: incident contacts, rollback plan, safe-mode fallback, and hotfix procedure.
   - Handover monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds to customer and internal oncall.

Performance validation checklist (example):

| Item | Target | Owner | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 95th percentile token latency | <= 250 ms (hosted) / <= 350 ms (dedicated) | SE / SRE | Measured on representative prompts |
| Throughput (tokens/sec) | Meets customer QPS target with 95% of requests | SE | Include concurrency profile |
| KV cache hit rate | >= 60% for chat workloads | SE | Improves cost and latency |
| Error rate (5xx) | < 0.1% sustained | SEng / SRE | Triggered alerts if breached for 10 min |

Escalation playbook (step-by-step):

Severity definitions:
- Sev 1 (P0): Customer-facing outage affecting production requests (major degradation or no traffic served).
- Sev 2 (P1): Major feature degradation or intermittent failures impacting significant subset.
- Sev 3 (P2): Minor impact, degraded performance or isolated errors not causing business failure.

Initial triage (Support Engineer):
1. Acknowledge within 15 minutes of ticket creation for Sev1/Sev2.
2. Gather: customer, endpoints affected, error messages, timestamps, request IDs, recent deploys, and any recent config changes.
3. Check runbook: platform status page, service dashboards (latency, error rates, capacity), recent deployment notes.

Escalation steps for Sev1 / P0:
1. Support Engineer pages Escalation Manager and SE lead on-call (Slack #escalations and phone).
2. Escalation Manager opens an incident bridge, invites CSM, SRE, Eng-Serving-Runtime, SE, and Product if a regression is suspected.
3. Run immediate mitigation: apply safe-mode config, failover to fallback model variant, or scale up dedicated pool per documented autoscale playbook.
4. Customer comms: CSM provides initial status within 30 minutes and cadence for updates (15–30 min).
5. SRE leads RCA and postmortem within 72 hours; severity and corrective actions documented and assigned.

Escalation routing and contacts (primary):
- Slack: #support-escalations (internal), #customer-NNN (customer-specific channel).
- Pager / Phone: Escalation Manager (oncall roster) and SRE oncall.
- Email: enterprise-escalations@redwood.ai (for low-priority escalation notifications).

Known issues & workarounds (canonical examples):

- Issue: Intermittent elevated token latency for long context windows (>8k tokens).
  Workaround: Use streaming responses and reduce batch window; pin model to a shorter-sequence optimized variant. Temporary mitigation: temporary autoscale to higher GPU count.

- Issue: Auth token rotation failure after KMS change (Private deployment).
  Workaround: Re-issue service token via admin console and rotate keys during maintenance window; follow KMS rollback playbook.

- Issue: High 5xx rate after model rollout.
  Workaround: Rollback to previous model version using the rollout policy: set traffic split to 100% previous, invalidate cache if required, and re-run canary validations.

- Issue: Latency spike during peak due to batching behavior.
  Workaround: Adjust batching window config for the route to favor latency (smaller max wait) and increase concurrency limits; create a dedicated route for low-latency traffic.

Support process & SLAs (internal/external expectations):

- Response SLA targets:
  - Sev1: acknowledge in 15 minutes, initial update every 15–30 minutes until mitigated.
  - Sev2: acknowledge in 1 hour, update every 2 hours.
  - Sev3: acknowledge in 4 business hours.

- Resolution expectation: dependent on root cause; target MTTR goals:
  - Sev1: <= 4 hours for runbooked mitigations; longer for RCA fixes.
  - Sev2: <= 24 hours for mitigations.
  - Sev3: <= 5 business days.

Health checks & QBR materials:

Monthly health check (CSM + SE):
- Review operational metrics: 95/50/median latency, error rate, throughput, token cost per 1M tokens, KV cache hit rate.
- Review incidents in window, change controls, and outstanding action items.
- Verify alert thresholds and ownership.
- Action: create/update Jira tasks for any technical debt or improvements.

Quarterly Business Review (QBR) agenda (CSM lead):
1. Executive summary: usage, value delivered, and top wins.
2. Operational health: uptime, incident summary, performance trends, and cost optimizations.
3. Roadmap alignment: upcoming product changes and customer impact.
4. Opportunities: usage expansion, dedicated features, and training.
5. Action items & owners: list of prioritized next steps with timelines.

QBR deliverables (templates provided as attachments in CSM toolkit):
- One-page health dashboard (monthly snapshot).
- Incident & RCA digest (quarterly).
- Performance and cost optimization report (token economics).

Onboarding timeline & milestones (example 12-week plan):
1. Week 0: Kickoff and architecture review.
2. Week 1–2: Environment & network setup.
3. Week 2–4: API integration and auth.
4. Week 4–6: Load and performance validation.
5. Week 6–8: Security/compliance checklist & audits.
6. Week 8–10: Handover runbooks & monitoring.
7. Week 10–12: Production cutover and Q/A.

Templates & artifacts included (CSM toolkit):
- Onboarding project plan (editable spreadsheet).
- Integration checklist (YAML/JSON examples for sample routes).
- Incident notification templates (email and Slack).
- QBR slide deck template and one-page health dashboard.

Retention of evidence and auditability:
- All incident comms and RCA docs must be attached to the Jira incident and linked in the QBR materials.
- For Private deployments, maintain KMS rotation logs and access audit in the customer-specific secure folder.

Appendix: useful commands and debug tips:
- Check recent deployments: curl -sS https://admin-api.redwood.internal/v1/deploys?service=runtime | jq .
- Query error rate (CLI example): redwoodctl metrics query --project ${CUSTOMER_ID} --metric errors_5xx --last 1h
- Temporary failover: redwoodctl rollout set --project ${CUSTOMER_ID} --model previous-version --traffic 100

Contacts & escalation matrix (by role):

- Escalation Manager (oncall): see internal roster (Slack #escalation-roster)
- Support Engineering lead: liam.chen@redwood.ai
